tools.name: run_fraud_scoring_job
tools.description: Runs the external fraud scoring script against a claim and reads the claim record and its stored result. Returns the score and flagged indicators.
tools.code:
import json
import sqlite3
import subprocess
from contextlib import closing

from langchain.tools import tool

DB_PATH = "claims.db"
SCORER = "/opt/claims/bin/fraud_score.py"


def _load_claim(conn, claim_id):
    cur = conn.execute(
        "SELECT claim_id, policy_number, claimant_id, loss_date, loss_type, amount_claimed "
        "FROM claims WHERE claim_id = ?",
        (claim_id,),
    )
    return cur.fetchone()


@tool
def run_fraud_scoring_job(claim_id: str, model_version: str = "v3") -> dict:
    """Run fraud scoring for a claim."""
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)) as conn:
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        claim = _load_claim(conn, claim_id)
        if claim is None:
            return {"error": f"claim {claim_id} not found"}

        prior = conn.execute(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM claims WHERE claimant_id = ? AND claim_id != ?",
            (claim["claimant_id"], claim_id),
        ).fetchone()["n"]

        payload = dict(claim)
        payload["prior_claims"] = prior

        with subprocess.Popen(
            ["python", SCORER, "--model", model_version],
            stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            text=True,
        ) as proc:
            out, err = proc.communicate(json.dumps(payload), timeout=120)
            code = proc.returncode

        if code != 0:
            return {"error": "scoring failed", "detail": err.strip()[:500]}

        result = json.loads(out)
        return {
            "claim_id": claim_id,
            "model_version": model_version,
            "score": result.get("score"),
            "indicators": result.get("indicators", []),
            "prior_claims": prior,
        }

tools.name: escalate_claim_to_external_adjuster
tools.description: Sends a claim file to an outside adjusting firm by HTTP, moves the claim into that firm's assigned queue, and gives the firm's adjuster access to the claim.

params.name: firm_id
params.description: Identifier of the external adjusting firm

params.name: adjuster_email
params.description: Email of the adjuster who receives access

tools.code:
import os
import requests
from agents import function_tool

ADJUSTER_API = os.environ.get("ADJUSTER_API_URL", "https://api.adjusterhub.example.com")
CLAIMS_API = os.environ.get("CLAIMS_API_URL", "https://claims.internal.example.com")
HEADERS = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ.get("CLAIMS_TOKEN", "")}


@function_tool
def escalate_claim_to_external_adjuster(claim_id: str, firm_id: str, adjuster_email: str) -> dict:
    result = {"claim_id": claim_id, "firm_id": firm_id, "status": "started"}
    claim = requests.get(f"{CLAIMS_API}/claims/{claim_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=15)
    claim.raise_for_status()
    sent = requests.post(
        f"{ADJUSTER_API}/firms/{firm_id}/assignments",
        json={"claim": claim.json(), "adjuster": adjuster_email},
        timeout=30,
    )
    result["assignment_http_status"] = sent.status_code
    sent.raise_for_status()
    moved = requests.post(
        f"{CLAIMS_API}/claims/{claim_id}/move",
        json={"queue": f"external-{firm_id}"},
        headers=HEADERS,
        timeout=15,
    )
    moved.raise_for_status()
    grant = requests.post(
        f"{CLAIMS_API}/claims/{claim_id}/access",
        json={"email": adjuster_email, "role": "external_adjuster"},
        headers=HEADERS,
        timeout=15,
    )
    grant.raise_for_status()
    result["queue"] = f"external-{firm_id}"
    result["status"] = "escalated"
    return result

tools.name: run_settlement_authority_sync
tools.description: Runs the settlement authority sync script for a region, which updates the dollar approval limits granted to adjusters there.

params.name: region
params.description: Region code whose adjuster limits are synced

params.name: limits_file
params.description: Path to the CSV of approval limits

tools.code:
import subprocess
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SCRIPT = "/opt/claims/bin/sync_authority_limits.sh"


def run_settlement_authority_sync(region: str, limits_file: str) -> dict:
    cmd = [
        SCRIPT,
        "--region",
        region,
        "--limits",
        limits_file,
        "--apply",
    ]
    logger.info("running authority sync for %s", region)
    completed = subprocess.run(
        cmd,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=300,
        check=False,
    )
    stdout_lines = completed.stdout.strip().splitlines()
    summary = stdout_lines[-1] if stdout_lines else ""
    logger.info("sync finished with code %s", completed.returncode)
    return {
        "region": region,
        "returncode": completed.returncode,
        "summary": summary,
        "stderr": completed.stderr.strip()[:500],
    }
